facts.fact: The Adwave article states that email marketing often returns $36 for every $1 spent, without naming a source for this figure.
facts.quote: It consistently delivers an incredible return, often bringing in **$36 for every $1 spent**.

facts.fact: The Adwave article estimates that by 2026, 392.5 billion emails will be sent every day to 4.6 billion users, attributing the figure to an unnamed estimate.
facts.quote: By 2026, the world will see an estimated **392.5 billion emails** sent every single day to **4.6 billion users**.

facts.fact: The Adwave article states that segmented and personalized emails are responsible for 58% of all revenue from email marketing.
facts.quote: segmented and personalized emails are responsible for **58% of all revenue** from email marketing.

facts.fact: The Adwave page states that a personalized subject line can increase email open rates by 50%.
facts.quote: A personalized subject line can increase open rates by a staggering **50%**

facts.fact: The Adwave page states that a tailored call-to-action can improve email conversions by 42%.
facts.quote: a tailored call-to-action can improve conversions by **42%**

facts.fact: The Adwave page cites unnamed 'recent studies' saying consumers tend to spend 34% more when they have personalized experiences.
facts.quote: consumers tend to spend **34%** more when they have personalized experiences

facts.fact: The Adwave page states that 10% of users say they actively dislike emails that feel generic.
facts.quote: a full **10%** of users say they actively dislike emails that feel generic

facts.fact: The Adwave page states that more than half of all emails are now opened on a phone.
facts.quote: More than half of all emails are now opened on a phone.

facts.fact: The Adwave page recommends a body text font size of at least 14px for email.
facts.quote: A font size of at least **14px** for your body text is a good rule of thumb.

facts.fact: The Adwave page says a welcome series is typically 3-5 emails sent over the first week.
facts.quote: A welcome series, typically **3-5 emails** sent over the first week

facts.fact: In the Adwave welcome series example, Email 2 is sent on Day 2, Email 3 on Day 4, and Email 4 on Day 6.
The Adwave page recommends sending the first abandoned cart reminder 1-4 hours after abandonment.
facts.quote: **Email 1 (1-4 hours after abandonment):** Send a gentle, low-pressure reminder.

facts.fact: The Adwave page recommends sending the second abandoned cart email 24 hours later, optionally with a 10% discount as an incentive.
facts.quote: **Email 2 (24 hours later):** Create a little urgency or sweeten the deal. A small incentive, like a **10% discount**

facts.fact: The Adwave page recommends a re-engagement campaign for subscribers who have not opened an email in 90 days.
facts.quote: I recommend sending this to anyone who hasn't opened one of your emails in **90 days**.

facts.fact: Adwave states its platform places ads on over 100 premium channels, targeting local viewers.
facts.quote: It then gets your ad on over **100 premium channels**, targeting local viewers who are most likely to walk through your door or visit your site.

facts.fact: The page cites some studies finding that 30% of companies see a return of $36 to $50 for every $1 spent on email marketing; this is a third-party claim, not an Adwave figure.
facts.unit: % of companies; USD return per $1 spent
facts.quote: some studies show **30% of companies** see a return between **$36 and $50 for every $1 spent**.

facts.fact: The page says many top email platforms offer free plans that typically allow up to 1,000 subscribers; this is a general statement about email platforms, not a specific Adwave plan.
facts.quote: they typically let you have up to **1,000 subscribers** and send thousands of emails a month for free.
